data.exact_reserve_text: During 2022, gross ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2020 and prior) increased by $95.6m due to strengthening of Syndicate 1919 reserves on long tail classes, following a review of the assumptions underlying IBNR estimates during the year. On a net basis ultimate claims have reduced by $162.7m due to the LPT that is discussed in more detail on page 5.

prior_year_events.event_name: Adverse prior year development on longer tail classes
prior_year_events.impact_description: Adverse prior year development on longer tail classes (2017 and prior) identified as a material driver of underwriting loss and remediation actions; led to strengthening of reserves on long-tail classes

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2022 was $885.053m. During 2022 gross ultimate claims for prior underwriting years (2020 and prior) increased by $95.6m, reflecting a strengthening of reserves on long-tail classes following a review and recalibration of IBNR assumptions and in the context of heightened inflationary pressures. Net ultimate claims reduced by $162.7m due to the Loss Portfolio Transfer (LPT) completed with SIRL. The movement is therefore a gross strengthening driven by IBNR recalibration and adverse prior development concentrated in long-tail casualty-type business.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Statement of Financial Position (Technical provisions - Claims outstanding, prior year column). Prior year development (gross) comes from explicit narrative sentence on page 49 stating a $95.6m increase for 2020 and prior. Figures in the report are presented in $000; converted here to millions. Claims development triangle is present but the printed table in the provided extract is partially ambiguous for per-cell extraction; triangle rows were not reliably parsed into numeric development rows for automated diagonal analysis. LPT materially affects net recoverables; gross and net movements diverge (gross strengthening vs net reduction). LOB attribution of the $95.6m is not quantified in the report; casualty/third party liability is inferred as the primary long-tail impacted line.
